destination.title: Two men dressed as police emptied a Boston museum

short20: It's called the biggest art heist in history — and the empty frames still hang on the wall.
Two men dressed as police talked their way into the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, handcuffed the guards in the basement, and were inside about eighty-one minutes.
They took thirteen works — cutting a Rembrandt and a Vermeer right out of their frames.
The haul is estimated around half a billion dollars, though the art is unsellable.
Not one of the thirteen has ever been found.
The FBI says it believes it knows who did it, but never named them, and says they are now dead.
The time to charge the theft has run out; there's a standing ten-million-dollar reward.
And the empty frames still hang exactly where the paintings were.
Watch the full story on the channel.

lines.text: Professional art thieves tend to be surgical. They take the most valuable, most portable pieces and leave the rest. These thieves did the opposite.
source_lines: Professional art thieves, the kind who steal to order, tend to be surgical: they take the most valuable, most portable pieces and leave the rest.
These thieves did something closer to the opposite.

lines.text: They damaged masterpieces by cutting them out. They skipped works of immense value hanging nearby. Decades later, investigators and historians still cannot fully explain the logic.

shorts.angle: The FBI followed the paintings out of Boston as far as Philadelphia, and then lost them completely.
shorts.type: B - what remains unrecovered, and who the offer is aimed at now
shorts.avoids: short20 says the FBI believes it knows who did it and that the men are dead. It never follows the art itself, or explains that the standing offer is now aimed at whoever is quietly holding it.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Ten million dollars has been sitting on the table for years. Why has nobody taken it?
shorts.loop_join: L5 stops on the open question of where the art went, and L1 answers it with the route the FBI says it traced out of Boston.

lines.text: The FBI has said it traced the stolen works out of Boston, to Connecticut, then to the Philadelphia area.
source_lines: It said the investigation traced the stolen works out of Boston — to Connecticut, and then to the Philadelphia area.

lines.text: It said that, roughly a decade before its 2013 announcement, some of the art was offered for sale there. Then the trail goes cold.
source_lines: And it said that, roughly a decade before the 2013 announcement, some of the art had been offered for sale in Philadelphia.
After that, the trail goes cold.

lines.text: Stolen art that cannot be sold openly drifts through a hidden world, passed between people who have every reason never to talk.
source_lines: Stolen art that cannot be sold openly tends to drift through a hidden world — used as collateral, as a favor, as a chip in some other deal, passed from hand to hand by people who have every reason never to talk.

lines.text: Each time it changes hands, fewer people hold the secret. A painting can be hidden in a room. The truth about it can be hidden inside a single person.
source_lines: Each time it changes hands, the knowledge of where it sits gets thinner, and the people who hold the secret get fewer.
A painting can be hidden in a single room.
The truth about where it went can be hidden inside a single person — and people do not last forever.

lines.text: The trail ran hot and useless at once. Thousands of tips. Psychics. Con men who wanted a price.
source_lines: In the early years, the trail was hot and useless at the same time.
Thousands of tips. Psychics. Con men claiming they could get the paintings back — for a price.

lines.text: Investigators went public with a website, images of every missing work, and billboards where the trail last ran warm.
source_lines: To shake something loose, investigators went public in a way they rarely do.
They launched an appeal to the whole country — a dedicated website, images of every missing work, even billboards in the region where the trail had last been warm.

lines.text: The art may sit in an attic, a storage unit, a basement, held by someone afraid of it.
source_lines: The second is that the art is still out there — sitting in an attic, a storage unit, a basement — held by someone who inherited it, or is afraid of it, or simply does not know what they have.

lines.text: The offer is no longer aimed at the thieves. Prosecutors say they want the works back far more than they want anyone in a cell. So where did the art go?
source_lines: we are far more interested in getting these works back than in putting you in a cell
